topic: HDFC Bank Analysis: From Long-Term Wealth Creation to Fibonacci Retracements
teaching_objective: Explain how to combine fundamental analysis with technical Fibonacci levels for entering a long-term position, using HDFC Bank as an educational case study.

slides.headline: HDFC Bank: Fundamentals + Technicals (Case Study)
slides.core_explanation: When investing in a giant compounder like HDFC Bank, finding the right entry point matters. By combining strong fundamentals (like post-merger stabilizing NIMs) with Fibonacci Retracements, you can spot high-probability accumulation zones. This is an educational analysis, not a buy/sell recommendation.

slides.headline: The 50% & 61.8% Golden Zones
slides.core_explanation: Fibonacci retracement levels (like 50% and 61.8%) act as natural support during a market pullback. Instead of chasing the stock at an all-time high, smart money waits for the price to 'retrace' to these golden zones before accumulating.

slides.headline: The 'Wait and Watch' Strategy
slides.core_explanation: No indicator is 100% accurate. If HDFC breaks below the 61.8% level, the trend may be reversing. Always combine Fibonacci with volume profile analysis and overall market conditions. Learn to wait patiently for your setup.
